extracted.intended_audience: rulers, aspiring princes, statesmen, and readers of political strategy
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and practical standards for acquiring, consolidating, and retaining princely power (military, political, and personal conduct), illustrated by the life and maxims of Castruccio. Intended as guidance for rulers on when to use force, deception, prudence, and public measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the measure of your strength
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is of the greatest important in this world that a man should know himself, and the measure of his own strength and means."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess honestly what resources, abilities, and support you have before undertaking enterprises; choose objectives that match your capacity. Example/advice to successor Pagolo: do not aspire beyond what you can maintain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt rule to your military aptitude
rubrics_metrics.description: "he who knows that he has not a genius for fighting must learn how to govern by the arts of peace."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you lack aptitude for warfare, compensate by governing through diplomacy, alliances, administration, and other peaceful arts rather than seeking military glory beyond your means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on your own resources, not distant powers
rubrics_metrics.description: "In the Emperor and in the princes of Milan thou canst place no reliance, for they are far distant, slow, and their help is very long in coming."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overdependence on distant or slow-to-act allies; build self-reliance through local forces, prestige, and internal organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert martial glory into political security
rubrics_metrics.description: Use recent victory and reputation to negotiate favourable terms and alliances rather than to expand recklessly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After major victories, seek to secure gains by diplomacy (e.g., 'you will be assisted to come to terms with the Florentines' using prestige). The timely use of leniency and treaties can stabilize holdings a victor cannot permanently garrison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit internal divisions and cultivate rival factions
rubrics_metrics.description: Castruccio maintained secret communications with both Bianchi and Neri in Pistoia and promised assistance to both sides, admitting leaders as 'friends' to gain control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Play opposing internal factions against one another; cultivate contacts on multiple sides, exploit factional distrust to create openings for intervention or takeover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use deception, fraud, and selective cruelty when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: "ready to play false with the unfaithful, and willing to overcome by fraud those whom he desired to subdue"; he 'wiped out all those who by their ambition might aspire to the principality', and used prisoners' towers to build a fortress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to deceive and punish enemies or untrustworthy allies when required to secure your position; use calculated cruelty to deter rivals, but balance it with clemency where it serves stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure popular support by relieving public needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Castruccio restored order in Rome chiefly by sending large quantities of corn by sea and removing the source of the trouble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address immediate economic or subsistence needs (food, safety) to win obedience and legitimacy; public provisioning can be as effective as force in pacifying unrest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize administrative and military systems for rapid mobilization
rubrics_metrics.description: He divided his country districts into five parts, supplied them with arms, and enrolled men under captains and ensigns to quickly bring twenty thousand soldiers into the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure territorial administration and recruitment so that forces can be raised quickly without relying solely on allies; prearranged command structures and provisioning are essential for defense and expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose battlefields and tactics that negate enemy numerical advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: Castruccio selected Serravalle (narrow pass/hill) to enable a smaller force to defeat a much larger army by advantage of position, surprise, and flanking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer terrain that channels or constrains larger forces, seize key positions in advance, use surprise (night operations), reserve forces for decisive flanking attacks, and exploit choke-points to neutralize enemy numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ surprise and coordinated multi-pronged attacks
rubrics_metrics.description: He seized the castle night before and marched silently to occupy the hill; he deployed infantry and cavalry along different approaches and ordered a flanking force to join a mounted detachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan simultaneous movements (hidden insertion, disciplined night marches) so that enemy reconnaissance and contingent cohesion are disrupted; coordinate infantry and cavalry to exploit confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use calculated restraint and display to maintain authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Castruccio was 'delightful among friends, but terrible to his enemies; just to his subjects', and celebrated victories with feasts, games, and medals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance affability toward supporters and subjects with firmness toward opponents; celebrate and publicize victories (medals, spectacles, distribution of spoils) to enhance prestige and loyalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overextension; prefer smaller secure state to larger insecure dominion
rubrics_metrics.description: "I should have been content with the governorships of Lucca and Pisa... I would have left thee, if a smaller state, at least with fewer enemies and perils."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt, consolidate and secure what you can govern effectively rather than pursuing expansion that invites persistent hostility and instability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit opportunity and act decisively when advantage appears
rubrics_metrics.description: Castruccio repeatedly took advantage of political upheaval (Pisan rebellion, betrayal) and moved quickly to capitalize on openings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be ready to act swiftly when rivals show weakness or popular sentiment shifts; hesitation may forfeit opportunities that can be seized by decisive measures.
